content.user_title: Adapt AI Workflows with Behavioral Modes
content.value_statement: AI assistants can give mismatched responses when task intent is unclear. This skill routes work into modes for planning, coding, debugging, review, teaching, shipping, and agent collaboration.
actual_capabilities: Defines seven task modes for brainstorming, implementation, debugging, review, teaching, shipping, and exploration.
Provides trigger phrases that help select the right mode from user intent.
Sets output formats for brainstorming options, debug analysis, reviews, lessons, and ship checklists.
Encourages implementation responses that are direct, complete, and production focused.
Describes planner, executor, and critic roles for multi-agent collaboration.
limitations: Does not execute commands, run tests, or deploy software by itself.
Does not include scripts, templates, or automation files beyond SKILL.md.
Relies on the assistant to infer the correct mode from the user request.
References clean-code standards but does not bundle a separate clean-code skill.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Direction
use_cases.description: Use brainstorm mode to compare product options, tradeoffs, and follow-up questions before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Fix a Production Bug
use_cases.description: Use debug mode to structure symptoms, likely causes, fixes, and prevention steps for a failing workflow.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Release Review
use_cases.description: Use ship and review modes to check quality, security, performance, and release readiness before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Mode
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for selecting the right behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use behavioral modes. Decide the best mode for this request, then answer in that mode: [describe my task].

prompt_templates.title: Brainstorm Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Explore early ideas before committing to a solution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use brainstorm mode for this feature idea. Give at least three options with pros, cons, and one recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Debug with Root Cause
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigate an error with evidence and prevention.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use debug mode. Analyze these symptoms, identify the likely root cause, propose a fix, and add prevention steps.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Plan Execute Critic
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for complex implementation work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the plan-execute-critic pattern. First plan atomic steps, then implement, then review for security, performance, and correctness.

output_examples.input: Brainstorm ways to improve onboarding for a developer tool.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists multiple approaches, compares pros and cons, and asks which direction should be explored next.

output_examples.input: Debug why login fails after a deployment.
output_examples.output: The assistant separates symptoms, root cause, fix, and prevention so the investigation stays focused.

output_examples.input: Review this pull request before release.
output_examples.output: The assistant groups review notes by severity and checks quality, security, performance, and readiness.

best_practices: Name the desired mode when the task has a clear workflow.
Provide error messages, files, or constraints before using debug or review mode.
Use ship mode only after core implementation work is complete.
anti_patterns: Do not use implement mode when you still need broad product exploration.
Do not expect this skill to run commands or verify tests directly.
Do not mix several modes in one prompt unless the workflow order is clear.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It defines task-specific AI behavior modes for planning, coding, debugging, reviewing, teaching, shipping, and agent collaboration.

faq.question: Does it execute commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill only provides behavioral guidance and declares read-oriented tools.

faq.question: Can I force a specific mode?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for brainstorm, implement, debug, review, teach, ship, explore, or plan-execute-critic behavior.

faq.question: Which tools support it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it useful for non-code work?
faq.answer: Yes. Brainstorm, teach, review, and planning modes can support documentation, product, and communication tasks.

faq.question: What should I provide for debug mode?
faq.answer: Provide symptoms, error messages, reproduction steps, recent changes, and expected behavior.
